findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: explorer_contract, read_doc, search_docs · Private data: audit_token_approvals, explorer_address, explorer_contract, explorer_search, explorer_stats, explorer_token, explorer_token_balances, explorer_token_holders, explorer_token_transfers, network_incidents · Public sink: explorer_token_holders, mempool_status, mining_stats, network_health, network_trends, supply_info · Destructive: network_health, network_nodes.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: explorer_contract, read_doc, search_docs · Private data: audit_token_approvals, explorer_address, explorer_contract, explorer_search, explorer_stats, explorer_token, explorer_token_balances, explorer_token_holders, explorer_token_transfers, network_incidents · Public sink: explorer_token_holders, mempool_status, mining_stats, network_health, network_trends, supply_info · Destructive: network_health, network_nodes

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
